findings.title: One `cwd` plays four roles today; the PR review splits them and the document never says how
findings.description:
The Envisioned State hands "range, working directory, and PR metadata to the existing code review" as if working directory were one value. In the current review package a single `cwd` is all of these at once:
- **Git root** for every `run_git` call.
- **Config root** for `get_config(..., cwd=...)`.
- **Rules root**: `resolve_rules_dir` probes `{cwd}/rules` and `{cwd}/.claude/rules`.
- **Persistence root**: `REVIEWS_DIR` is relative to the process cwd, and `save_review_result` stamps `resolve_reviewed_sha(".")`.

A tool-enabled PR review needs the tool root in the scratch worktree, but config, persistence and rules trust anchored in the operator's checkout. That split touches `review_client.py`, `rules.py`, `resolution*.py` and `persistence.py`. It contradicts "from that point the review path is the existing one" and Related Work's "all reused; none changed in shape". The document should name the split (tool root versus project root) as an explicit principle and assign it to a slice.

findings.title: Rules loading in the scratch worktree lets the PR author supply the reviewer's rules
findings.description:
"Rules outside a planned project" says an unplanned repository gets "the template's rules and language auto-detection only". That is not what `resolve_rules_dir` does: with no CLI flag or config, it falls through to `{cwd}/rules`, `{cwd}/.claude/rules`, then `~/.config/squadron/rules`.

If `cwd` is the scratch worktree, those directories are the PR head's content, written by a third party. They would be injected as trusted review rules, and the result posted under the operator's identity. The document treats title, body and threads as untrusted but is silent on rules and other repo-resident instruction files read from the head tree. It must state where rules come from for a PR review (base ref, operator checkout, or user config; never the head tree) and correct the description of the fallback chain.

findings.title: Base ref is never fetched, and the reviewed sha is stamped from the wrong HEAD
findings.description:
"Base semantics" requires merge-base-to-head "so the review matches what the host displays", but only the head is fetched ("Fetching without checkout"). Three gaps follow:
- **Stale base.** A stale local base branch gives a different merge-base than the host. "Base moved since resolution" is listed as a failure mode, but no mechanism detects it.
- **Shallow or partial clones.** These are common in enterprise checkouts and can have no merge-base at all. They are not in the enumerated failure modes.
- **Wrong sha.** The existing stamp is `git rev-parse HEAD` in the process cwd, which is the operator's checkout, not the PR head. The document says "the head sha recorded in the artifact is what was reviewed" without noting this must be replaced by the PR record's head sha. It also does not say whether `sq review resolve`, which diffs against `reviewedSha`, is supported on a PR-keyed artifact.

findings.title: Target grammar admits PRs the local repository cannot review, and rejects the common fork setup
findings.description:
The grammar accepts a full URL and `owner/repo#n`, yet the adapter's contract is "a head ref present in the local repository". Behaviour when the target names a repository other than the cwd's is undefined.

Resolution must also "fail loudly when the repository… has more than one" host remote. `origin` plus `upstream` is the standard fork layout in the enterprise setting the Motivation names, so the primary audience hits a hard error on the bare-number and no-argument forms. A bare number is also ambiguous with a numeric branch name. The document needs a remote-selection rule and a stated answer for cross-repository targets (refuse, or fetch by URL).

findings.title: "Persistence takes a target" changes a contract the pipeline shares, against the stated scope
findings.description:
Scope says "no pipeline actions… no executor changes" and Envisioned State says "the pipeline `review` action… unchanged". But `persistence.py` is declared "shared between CLI review commands and pipeline review actions", and `SliceInfo` is consumed in `pipeline/actions/review.py` and `review/template_inputs.py` as well as the CLI.

`format_review_markdown` hardcodes slice assumptions: `slice:` and `project:` frontmatter, the `# Review: … — slice {index}` heading, and silent `"unknown"` / `0` fallbacks that the project's no-silent-fallback rule forbids extending. Making the target generic means either editing those shared signatures (pipeline code changes) or adding a parallel PR formatter (which breaks "a slice-keyed target and a PR-keyed target satisfy the same contract"). The document should say which.

The claim that "archiving, digest, and integrity checks… apply unchanged" also needs checking. `archive_existing_review` relies on the reviews directory being scanned non-recursively by Context Forge and metrology, which says nothing about a squadron data directory.

findings.title: Slice order makes `sq review pr` claim flag parity before a PR review can be saved
findings.description:
Slice 2 (`sq review pr`) promises "full parity with the existing review flags", which includes the save flags. PR-keyed persistence is slice 3 and is gated on 916 and 917 landing on `main`, an external dependency with no stated status.

In between, `sq review pr` must either not save (a parity violation) or fabricate a minimal `SliceInfo`, the pattern the principles explicitly refuse to extend. Either move persistence ahead of the command, or state that slice 2 ships without save and fails explicitly when save is requested.

findings.title: Unplanned-repository storage location is an undefined config key with no identity scheme
findings.description:
"A configured squadron data directory" does not exist today; squadron has `~/.config/squadron/` conventions but no such key. Three things are undefined:
- **Unset key.** Project rules require an explicit error or a centrally defined default, not an implicit one.
- **Naming.** "A PR-keyed name" must carry host, owner and repo, not just the number, or PR 12 from two repositories collides in a shared directory.
- **Lookup.** How posting and `sq pr create` ("the latest saved review") find artifacts there is not described.

"Planned project" detection is also unspecified (presence of `project-documents/`, a `cf` project, or both). It gates persistence, rules and scope behaviour, so it needs a single definition.

findings.title: `sq pr create` has a section no input supports, and skips the push
findings.description:
- **Unsupported section.** The fixed body includes "how it was verified", and the design goal says "nothing is asserted that no input supports". None of the named inputs (commits, slice design and tasks, saved review) records test or verification evidence. A one-shot model call asked to fill a mandatory section with no source will invent one. Either name the input, or define the section's explicit empty form.
- **Push.** Creating a PR requires the branch on the remote. The document never says whether squadron pushes, requires a pushed and up-to-date branch, or fails. `gh pr create` prompts interactively when the branch is unpushed, which hangs a subprocess call.
- **Existing PR.** Behaviour when an open PR already exists for the branch is not stated.
- **Stale review.** "Latest saved review" has no freshness rule. A review whose `reviewedSha` is not the branch head would be reported as provenance for code it never saw.
- **Non-slice branches.** No PR-keyed review can exist before the PR does, so "latest saved review" is empty for them. That should be stated as the expected case.

findings.title: Scratch worktree lifecycle is deferred, yet it carries the "operator's checkout is untouched" guarantee
Posting idempotency and stale-head handling are stated as outcomes without a mechanism
findings.description:
- **Update versus supersede.** "Updates or supersedes rather than stacking" leaves open a choice with different consequences. Editing in place erases the record of what was said about an earlier head sha. Superseding needs a rule for the old comment.
- **Finding the prior comment.** "Marked so squadron can find… its own prior comment" relies on text in a user-editable body. It must also match on author login (the reason `identify the operator` is in the protocol) and page through all comments. Two operators posting on the same PR is an unaddressed case.
- **Stale head.** "A review posted against a PR whose head has since moved must say so" requires re-resolving the PR at post time. The flow describes resolve, review, save, post as one pass with no second resolution.
- **Post-only path.** It is not stated whether a previously saved review can be posted without re-running the review, although "the saved review is rendered" implies posting reads the artifact.

findings.title: Protocol surface is sized for hypothetical hosts, and first-cut scope is wider than the motivation needs
findings.description:
The motivating pain is four manual steps: checkout, find base, run `--diff`, paste result. The architecture adds more than that needs:
- **Five-form target grammar.** Number, URL and current branch cover the motivation; defer `owner/repo#n` and branch-name lookup.
- **Linked issues and unresolved threads as prompt inputs.** `gh` has no first-class command for thread resolution state. It needs `gh api graphql` with pagination, which is the most host-specific shape in the design. It sits directly against "the protocol must not leak `gh`-specific shapes", and other hosts model it differently. Title and body are enough for a first cut.
- **One six-operation protocol.** Resolve, fetch head, read threads, post comment, create PR and identify operator are in one interface with one implementation. Read-only review consumers depend on write operations they never call. Split read and write, or grow the protocol per slice instead of fixing it in the keystone slice.
- **A separate parity slice** for slash commands, which the "CLI is the contract" principle already makes thin transports. Fold it into the command slices.

findings.title: `sq doctor` check needs a stated severity for operators who never use PRs
findings.description: The Constraint says "no PR is ever required", but doctor "gains checks for the host adapter (`gh` present, authenticated, host reachable)". If those fail doctor's exit status, every operator without `gh` gets a failing doctor. State that they are informational unless PR features are used. "Host reachable" is also a network call inside a preflight, and which host it checks is undefined when run outside a repository.
